video.description:
Learn to explain keeping app data in one place: State Management, Unidirectional Data Flow & Reducer, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
State Management - The way an app stores and updates the data that its screens show.
Unidirectional Data Flow - A design where data moves in one direction and every change starts from an action.
Reducer - A function that takes the current state and an action and returns the new state.

Quiz at the end - write your answers in the comments, then watch again to check.

State Management - The way an app stores and updates the data that its screens show.
한국어: State Management: 앱이 화면에 보여 줄 데이터를 저장하고 갱신하는 방식

Unidirectional Data Flow - A design where data moves in one direction and every change starts from an action.

Reducer - A function that takes the current state and an action and returns the new state.
한국어: Reducer: 현재 상태와 액션을 받아 새 상태를 돌려주는 함수

landscape.hook: Can you explain State Management, Unidirectional Data Flow and Reducer in English?

dialogue.title: Five places, one bug

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, our screens change the same data in five places. The bugs are strange.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That is a state management problem. You need one clear place for the data your screens show.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Use unidirectional data flow. The view sends an action, the state changes, and the view updates.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So data moves in only one direction?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes. No view edits the state directly.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then where do the changes happen?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: In a reducer. A reducer takes the current state and an action, and returns the new state.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Like `reduce` in our code, with `add` and `reset`?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Exactly. The same state and action always give the same result, so a reducer is easy to test.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Good state management makes everything easier to test.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: And unidirectional data flow makes bugs easy to trace.
Our state management is simple: one struct holds everything.
